title: Hierarchical canary architecture for pinned model replacements
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a hierarchical, multi-stage canary and A/B testing framework for model version swaps behind pins that explicitly separates performance verification (latency/cost), functional correctness (safety/accuracy), and user-experience signals (engagement/regression). The architecture should allow progressive exposure across tiers (synthetic-only, holdout microcohorts, region-limited ramps, and global A/B) and publish a standardized performance profile for each onboarded revision.

Why: Current pinned-swap playbooks rely on single-stage canaries and ad-hoc checks which makes rollbacks slow and conservative. A hierarchical approach reduces blast radius while giving product and platform teams clearer signal ownership. Publishing the performance profile as part of onboarding unlocks automated routing and more accurate cost predictions for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope: Design the verification tiers, gating metrics, traffic routing rules, experiment instrumentation, failure modes and rollback automation. Deliverables: spec doc, console UI hooks for tier configuration, telemetry dashboards, guardrails in routing layer, and a pilot with an internal API using 1-2 model families.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include full multi-tenant quota controls or billing changes; those will be separate work. It also does not cover on-prem upgrade mechanisms beyond basic API compatibility checks.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc approved with diagrams showing 4-tier exposure and transition criteria
Routing layer accepts a hierarchical canary config with tier definitions and metric gates
Console exposes a 'Pin rollout' workflow that maps pins -> tiers and displays gating state
Telemetry dashboards ingest required metrics and show pass/fail for each tier within 30 minutes of rollout
Pilot completed with one model family: canary triggered, metrics recorded, and automated rollback performed on injected failure
Published performance profile artifact (latency P50/P95, token cost, memory delta) available in model catalog for the pilot revision
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design/Spec (2 weeks): finalize tier definitions, gating metrics, and failure thresholds; proto console wireframes
Phase 1 - Routing + Telemetry (3 weeks): implement hierarchical canary config in routing layer + telemetry ingestion spec
Phase 2 - Console + UX (2 weeks): add UI to create a hierarchical rollout tied to an existing pin; show live gating state
Phase 3 - Pilot & Hardening (2 weeks): run internal pilot with staged exposure, record lessons, tighten thresholds
Phase 4 - Rollout to select customers (post-pilot): document runbook and enable via feature flag for Dedicated/private customers
metrics_and_gates: Performance gates: latency P95 increase <= 15% and absolute P95 < 350ms for low-latency SKUs
Cost gates: per-token CPU/GPU token cost delta <= 20% compared to baseline profile
Quality gates: task-specific f1/accuracy delta thresholds (example: summarization ROUGE delta <= 2 points), plus safety heuristic pass rate >= 99.5%
User-experience gates (A/B tiers): engagement delta within +/-2% over a 48h window for control vs variant
Operational gates: error rate HTTP 5xx increase < 0.1% absolute; KV cache hit-rate not decreased by more than 5%
